newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin press office denies op delay rumours.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin press office denies op delay rumours.

text.p: The head of President Boris Yeltsin's press office on Tuesday denied reports on a Moscow radio station that Yeltsin was too sick to undergo planned heart surgery.
"This does not correspond to reality," Igor Ignatyev said, when asked about an Ekho Moskvy report that a bypass operation was too risky because Yeltsin's haemoglobin levels were too low.

The radio quoted sources at the Central Clinical Hospital, where Yeltsin, 65, is expected to undergo the operation, as saying his haemoglobin levels were so low that few surgeons would recomend an operation in the forseeable future.

The Ekho Moskvy report worried Russian financial markets, where traders are already wary about the impact Yeltsin's possible departure from the Russian political scene could have on economic reforms. Some share prices eased.
Yeltsin has been seen rarely in public since he was reelected for a second term in office on July 3. He said on September 5 that he had agreed to have a heart operation.
The non-stop rumour mill about the president's health has clearly annoyed the Kremlin which says Yeltsin is working at the Barvikha sanatorium.
Yeltsin met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov there on Tuesday.
A council of Russian and foreign doctors decided late last month that Yeltsin was fit enough for surgery, which could take place within next the two months.
